page.mentor_intro: Huntington disease has no disease-modifying therapy, so chorea management sits at the centre of what clinicians can actually offer. Chorea — random, jerk-like movements migrating between body parts — is the most common motor manifestation, interfering with daily activities, injuring patients and eroding quality of life. The therapeutic mainstay is VMAT2 inhibition: tetrabenazine's legacy is real efficacy weighed against depression and parkinsonism, while deutetrabenazine's deuterium substitution confers a longer half-life, less-frequent dosing and an improved tolerability profile — the reason it became the modern default.

teaching_points.claim: Chorea is defined as jerk-like movements moving randomly between body parts, caused by various disorders; current symptomatic therapy is quite effective, though few aetiology-targeted therapies exist.

Deutetrabenazine is FDA-approved for chorea in Huntington's disease; deuterium substitution gives a longer half-life allowing less-frequent daily dosing, and as a reversible VMAT2 inhibitor it depletes monoamines.

In Huntington's disease, an inherited neurodegenerative disorder with no disease-modifying treatment, chorea is the most common motor manifestation and may interfere with daily activities, reduce quality of life and cause injury.

uncertainties: Whether suppressing chorea with VMAT2 inhibitors alters long-term functional outcomes beyond symptom relief is unknown.
Treatment of the non-choreic motor and neuropsychiatric burden (bradykinesia, depression, suicidality) needs separate, individualised strategies.

page.mentor_intro: The hybrid closed loop system is the closest thing to an artificial pancreas that mainstream care currently has: a continuous glucose sensor feeding an algorithm that adjusts pump-delivered insulin in real time, with the user still announcing meals. Building on pump and CGM technology that already improves HbA1c, time-in-range and hypoglycaemia burden, closed loops reduce the daily cognitive load of type 1 diabetes. The field has now matured enough for network meta-analysis to compare competing systems head-to-head, which is exactly the evidence clinicians need when choosing between them.

teaching_points.claim: Diabetes technologies represent a paradigm shift in type 1 diabetes care: pumps and continuous glucose monitors improve HbA1c, enhance time in range, limit severe hypoglycaemia and reduce diabetes distress, and the artificial pancreas extends this trajectory.
A network meta-analysis of randomised trials compares the efficacy and safety of different hybrid closed loop systems, including the Minimed 670G class, across children, adolescents and adults.

Hybrid closed-loop systems automatically modulate basal insulin infusion in response to continuous interstitial glucose telemetry, significantly increasing time in range (70-180 mg/dL) toward target >70%.
Automated basal suspension during downward glucose trajectories substantially reduces nocturnal hypoglycemia compared to sensor-augmented pump therapy alone.

uncertainties: Long-term durability of glycaemic gains and real-world adherence outside trial conditions are less certain.
Which system performs best for which patient phenotype (hypoglycaemia-prone, adolescents, highly variable schedules) is being refined.

page.mentor_intro: Hydroxychloroquine is the closest thing SLE has to a foundation drug: almost universally recommended for its immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects, with benefits that extend beyond symptom control. Its liability is dose-limiting retinal toxicity — potentially irreversible, which makes early detection the whole game, and screening rather than blanket avoidance the accepted strategy. Balancing therapeutic levels against ocular safety, and layering cardiac monitoring for the QT-prolongation concern, is the core prescribing skill.

teaching_points.claim: Hydroxychloroquine has gained prominence in SLE treatment through a multifaceted mechanism of action as a lipophilic, lysosomotropic agent that accumulates in lysosomes and alkalinises them.
HCQ is a cornerstone of SLE therapy, but long-term exposure can cause potentially irreversible retinopathy in which early detection is critical.
To minimize lifetime risk of irreversible bull's-eye retinopathy, daily hydroxychloroquine dosing should not exceed 5.0 mg/kg actual body weight per day (AAO guidelines).

Annual retinal screening with spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and automated visual fields (10-2, or 24-2 in Asian patients) is recommended after 5 years of therapy, or earlier in high-risk patients.

uncertainties: Individual susceptibility to retinopathy varies unpredictably, so screening intervals and dose ceilings remain population-level rather than personalised.
Cardiac toxicity (QT prolongation, cardiomyopathy) monitoring practice is less standardised than retinal screening.
mcq_angles: HCQ mechanism and its SLE-specific benefits (flare reduction, survival data).
Retinopathy risk factors: dose, duration, renal impairment, tamoxifen co-exposure.
Screening tools: OCT, visual fields, and screening cadence.
QT/cardiac monitoring and drug interactions.

page.mentor_intro: Hydroxychloroquine retinopathy screening is one of the few areas where ophthalmology has produced precise, iterative, dose-anchored guidance — and then revised it as prevalence data changed. The Marmor-led AAO recommendations established the framework: toxicity is parafoveal in most patients, risk rises steeply with dose and duration, and OCT is the screening tool of choice. The 2025 revision updates that framework for current knowledge, while rheumatology-facing reviews translate the same evidence into prescribing behaviour: keep doses at or below the accepted ceiling, and screen on schedule rather than stopping a drug that most patients need.

teaching_points.claim: The 2025 AAO revision updates the hydroxychloroquine screening recommendations originally published a decade earlier, reflecting new knowledge about toxicity patterns.

The 2016 revision updated recommendations in light of new information about toxicity prevalence, risk factors, fundus distribution and screening-tool effectiveness, with the locus of damage parafoveal in most patients.
Research advances in HCQ retinopathy have direct implications for rheumatology care, where HCQ remains almost universally recommended in SLE and the toxicity is the major dose-limiting concern.

uncertainties: The retina typically remains clinically normal for many years, with unpredictable individual susceptibility defining residual risk.
Optimal screening intervals for very low-risk patients versus high-risk (renal impairment, tamoxifen) subgroups continue to be individualised.

page.mentor_intro: Hypercalcaemia is common — roughly 1% of the population — and its severity grading drives everything: mild hypercalcaemia is usually asymptomatic or vaguely constitutional, while severe hypercalcaemia is a medical emergency of dehydration, confusion, shortened QT and crisis-level calcium. The two questions that organise every case are 'how high' and 'why': primary hyperparathyroidism dominates the outpatient mild-to-moderate end of the spectrum, malignancy dominates the severe end, and the PTH level separates them in a single test.

teaching_points.claim: Primary hyperparathyroidism, the most common cause of hypercalcemia, is most often identified in postmenopausal women, with clinical presentation evolving over 40 years into distinct phenotypes.
Hypercalcemia affects approximately 1% of the worldwide population; mild hypercalcemia (total calcium <12 mg/dL) is usually asymptomatic but may cause fatigue and constipation in about 20%.
Primary hyperparathyroidism and malignancy account for over 90% of all hypercalcemia cases; elevated or inappropriately normal intact PTH confirms parathyroid-dependent hypercalcemia.

Initial emergency stabilization of symptomatic or severe hypercalcemia (>14 mg/dL [>3.5 mmol/L]) mandates vigorous isotonic saline hydration (200-300 mL/h) followed by intravenous bisphosphonates (zoledronic acid) or calcitonin.

uncertainties: Whether asymptomatic mild hypercalcaemia from PHPT always warrants parathyroidectomy is individualised by guidelines.
The calcium-adjustment formulas and ionised-calcium thresholds in hypoalbuminaemia vary in reliability.

PTH-based differential: PTH versus PTH-independent causes.
PHPT as the commonest cause; malignancy as the commonest severe cause.
Initial management: hydration, calcitonin, then bisphosphonate or denosumab.

page.mentor_intro: Hypercalcaemia of malignancy is the commonest metabolic complication of cancer and the commonest cause of hypercalcaemia in hospitalised patients, affecting over a quarter of patients with cancer across its phenotypes — humoral (PTHrP-driven), osteolytic, and the rarer calcitriol-secreting and ectopic-PTH forms. Acute management remains hydration plus an antiresorptive — bisphosphonate or denosumab — with treatment of the underlying malignancy as the definitive lever.

page.mentor_intro: The physiology of malignancy-associated hypercalcaemia explains its treatment: humoral hypercalcaemia mediated by PTHrP drives most cases, with osteolytic metastatic disease and calcitriol-secreting lymphomas completing the picture — and mixed PTHrP-plus-calcitriol elevations, once thought rare, are increasingly recognised across solid and haematological malignancies. Every therapy maps onto that physiology: aggressive saline rehydration restores the depleted extracellular volume, calcitonin lowers calcium within hours, and bisphosphonates or denosumab shut down the osteoclast-driven resorption that sustains it.

teaching_points.claim: Malignancy-associated hypercalcemia — the most common cause of hypercalcemia in the emergency department — arises from direct bone resorption by metastases, vitamin D-secreting malignancies, and increased PTH or PTHrP levels.

Concurrent elevations in PTHrP and calcitriol, initially considered rare and solid-tumour-associated, are increasingly detected in hypercalcemic patients across solid and hematologic malignancies, with diagnostic and therapeutic implications.

PTH-related protein (PTHrP) secretion accounts for ~80% of hypercalcemia of malignancy (humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy), characteristically producing high serum calcium with suppressed intact PTH and normal/low 1,25-(OH)2D.

Intravenous bisphosphonates (zoledronic acid 4 mg IV over 15 min) or denosumab (RANKL inhibitor) achieve sustained calcium normalization in >85% of malignancy cases, with denosumab preferred in renal impairment.

uncertainties: The diagnostic work-up of mixed-mechanism HCM is being re-evaluated as concurrent PTHrP/calcitriol elevations are recognised more often.
Whether earlier denosumab use in renal impairment changes outcomes versus cautious bisphosphonate use is practice-dependent.
mcq_angles: PTHrP physiology: why PTH is suppressed and why osteoclast activation is indirect.
Treatment timeline: saline (hours), calcitonin (days), bisphosphonate/denosumab (days to weeks).

page.mentor_intro: Hypercapnic respiratory failure — ventilatory failure producing a rising PaCO2, usually on a background of COPD, obesity or neuromuscular disease — is the one form of acute respiratory failure where non-invasive ventilation is not just an option but the standard of care that changed outcomes. The ERS/ATS guideline anchors NIV application across acute respiratory failure aetiologies, while the COPD-exacerbation literature supplies the clinical context: exacerbations drive disease progression, wellbeing and mortality, and correcting the hypercapnia early is what breaks the downward spiral.

teaching_points.claim: The ERS/ATS guideline provides recommendations for clinical application of noninvasive ventilation across aetiologies of acute respiratory failure, based on current literature.

COPD exacerbations — acute deterioration in respiratory symptoms — fundamentally impact disease progression, comorbidities, wellbeing and mortality, and carry the largest share of COPD's socioeconomic burden.
Arterial blood gas criteria identifying acute or acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure include PaCO2 > 45 mmHg with uncompensated acidemia (pH < 7.35).
Controlled oxygen therapy targeting SpO2 88-92% prevents worsening hypercapnia secondary to loss of hypoxic vasoconstriction (V/Q mismatch) and the Haldane effect.

uncertainties: NIV in hypercapnic failure from non-COPD causes (obesity-hypoventilation, neuromuscular) is extrapolated from thinner evidence.
The role of high-flow nasal oxygen as an alternative or bridge in milder hypercapnia is still being defined.

page.mentor_intro: In acute hypercapnic respiratory failure from a COPD exacerbation, NIV with bilevel support is the intervention with the strongest evidence in the whole of acute respiratory medicine — the Cochrane lineage showing it reduces acidosis, respiratory rate, intubation and mortality. But 'start NIV' is only half the competence: knowing the criteria that predict success, recognising failure early, and understanding where the newer evidence places high-flow nasal therapy relative to bilevel support is what separates protocol following from skilled management.

teaching_points.claim: NIV with bilevel positive airway pressure is commonly used and evidence-supported for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure secondary to COPD exacerbation, as evaluated in a systematic review.
A network meta-analysis compares non-invasive respiratory support modalities for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure, with treatment failure, all-cause mortality and intubation as outcomes.

Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (BIPAP) is the first-line therapy for COPD exacerbations with persistent respiratory acidosis (pH 7.25-7.35, PaCO2 > 45 mmHg) despite optimal medical therapy, reducing intubation rates by >60%.

Immediate indications for invasive mechanical ventilation over NIV include severe encephalopathy, hemodynamic instability, uncontrolled vomiting, high aspiration risk, or failure of pH to improve after 1-2 hours of NIV.

uncertainties: Patient-selection boundaries for NIV versus early intubation (severe acidosis, altered consciousness, comorbidity burden) remain judgement-heavy.
Where high-flow nasal therapy sits for milder hypercapnia or as NIV-tolerance rescue is being defined by comparative trials.
mcq_angles: NIV success predictors: pH threshold, conscious level, cooperation.
Failure criteria: worsening acidosis despite NIV, exhaustion, hypoxia.
Cochrane-evidenced benefits: mortality and intubation reduction.
